description.before: The SEN68 and SEN69C modules combine particulate sensing with humidity, temperature, VOC, NOx and formaldehyde measurements. SEN69C adds CO2 sensing; an evaluation kit is available for developers.
description.after:
Sensirion released the SEN68 and SEN69C modules for indoor air-quality equipment, combining particulate sensing with humidity, temperature, VOC, NOx and formaldehyde measurements.
SEN69C adds CO2 sensing.
Both use the new SPS6x miniaturised MEMS particulate-sensing component to fit multiple measurements into a compact module.

The modules and SEK-SEN69C evaluation kit are available through distributors.
The kit exposes the measurements and onboard algorithms for prototyping, but requires a separate SEK-SensorBridge to operate.
These are components for products such as room sensors and air purifiers, not a finished building-monitoring installation.

description.before: ETH researchers demonstrate light-emitting polymers that withstand lithographic processing, a step towards smaller OLED displays.
description.after:
ETH Zurich researchers developed light-emitting polymers that also act as photoresists, allowing OLED materials to be patterned with chipmaking techniques.
Reactive groups on the outside of each molecule cross-link under UV light, while a protective shell shields its light-emitting core from processing chemicals.

The team produced a 300 by 430 micrometre fluorescent test image and, separately, an electrically powered ETH logo measuring 1 by 2.4 millimetres.
The fluorescent image is not a display, and a working screen still requires electronics to control individual pixels independently.

caption.after: Microscopic fluorescent test image, 300 by 430 micrometres; not an electrically driven display. Image: Lo SW et al., Nature 2026 / ETH Zurich

description.before: Klarent develops AI agents that write and maintain software tests for web and mobile applications.
description.after:
Zurich-based Klarent raised USD 8 million in seed funding to expand into the US, grow its engineering team and develop its web and mobile testing platform.
Founded by former Google engineers Asheem Panakkat and Momchil Ivanov, the company names JD Sports, NZZ and Sixt among its customers.

Its agents use language models to write and adapt deterministic test code, rather than relying on an AI model to execute each test.
Klarent combines this automation with human review of results, aiming to reduce the work of maintaining tests as applications change.

description.before: UniSieve develops membranes for industrial gas separation and carbon capture.
description.after:
Zurich-based UniSieve raised USD 9 million in Series A funding, bringing its total funding to USD 25 million.
The company will use the capital to scale deployment of its gas-separation membranes and adapt them to additional industrial applications.

The membranes separate molecules through precisely sized pores, offering an alternative to energy-intensive thermal separation.
UniSieve says its systems have reached pre-commercial maturity in olefin separation and carbon capture at emission sources, with field-tested performance and repeatable manufacturing supporting the move towards broader commercial deployment.

description.before: Namespace builds compute infrastructure for coding, builds and tests across Linux, macOS and Windows.
description.after:
Namespace has raised USD 42M to expand its infrastructure for building and testing software. The platform runs development environments, GitHub Actions and build workloads on its own server racks, with support for Linux, Windows and macOS.

The funding will support product development and additional data-centre capacity, including a larger fleet of Mac hardware for iOS and macOS builds. Namespace reports more than 1,000 customers and eightfold revenue growth over the past year. The round brings its total funding to USD 65M, seven months after its Series A.

description.before: Cotierra builds reactors and monitoring software that turn agricultural residues into biochar.
description.after:
Cotierra raised EUR 2.6M to expand decentralised biochar production from pilots into repeatable, multi-year commercial deployments, initially in coffee supply chains.
The Zurich company combines reactors that turn agricultural residues into biochar near their source with software to operate, monitor and verify production.

Its system tracks production and application of biochar, which returns carbon-rich material to agricultural soils.
The financing announcement describes plans to expand across regions and agricultural supply chains; it does not quantify achieved carbon removal or crop-yield improvements.

description.before: Prevision Medicine develops tests that measure how a patient's living cancer cells respond to different treatments.
description.after:
Prevision Medicine has raised USD 5.4M to commercialise its cancer-treatment testing platform. Instead of relying only on how similar patients responded, the test exposes living cells from a patient's tumour to a library of treatments and measures their response.

The Zurich company plans to use the funding for regulatory clearances, reimbursement coverage and expansion across Europe. Its PrevisionOne test is intended to help clinicians evaluate treatment options for blood cancers and solid tumours, using measurements from the individual patient's cells.

description.before: Winduction's prototype charges an electric bus from a ground plate through coils integrated into its tyres, reducing the gap across which power must be transferred. The ETH spin-off aims to recharge buses at stops with smaller onboard batteries; passenger trials are planned for 2028, rather than already operating commercially.
description.after:
Winduction demonstrated an electric bus charging from a ground plate through coils in its tyres.
Moving the receiving coils into the wheel reduces the transmission gap compared with underbody charging.
The system needs specially developed steel-free tyres because conventional steel belts would absorb energy from the magnetic field as heat.

The company is building a laboratory and test bus stop in Winterthur before integrating the components for operation outside its private test area.
Passenger trials are planned for 2028, with Swiss transport operators still in discussions.
Smaller batteries and lower route costs are intended benefits, not results from a completed passenger-service trial.

caption.after: Wheel-based charging concept; the video includes animation. Video: ETH News for Industry
